statement: To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a medial rectangle.
heath_proof: Let the rational straight lines A, B, C commensurable in square only be set out; let D be taken a mean proportional between A, B, [VI. 13] and let it be contrived that, as B is to C, so is D to E. [VI. 12]  Since A, B are rational straight lines commensurable in square only, therefore the rectangle A, B, that is, the square on D [VI. 17], is medial. [X. 21] Therefore D is medial. [X. 21] And since B, C are commensurable in square only, and, as B is to C, so is D to E, therefore D, E are also commensurable in square only. [X. 11] But D is medial; therefore E is also medial. [X. 23, addition] Therefore D, E are medial straight lines commensurable in square only. I say next that they also contain a medial rectangle. For since, as B is to C, so is D to E, therefore, alternately, as B is to D, so is C to E. [V. 16] But, as B is to D, so is D to A; therefore also, as D is to A, so is C to E; therefore the rectangle A, C is equal to the rectangle D, E. [VI. 16] But the rectangle A, C is medial; [X. 21] therefore the rectangle D, E is also medial. Therefore medial straight lines commensurable in square only have been found which contain a medial rectangle.

10.28
**Statement:** To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a medial rectangle.

**Step 1.** Let three rational straight lines A, B, C be set out which are commensurable in square only, each with each: that is, any two of them have squares that are commensurable, while the lines themselves are incommensurable in length [D10.1.2].

**Step 2.** Let D be taken a mean proportional between A and B [6.13], so that A : D = D : B; and let E be taken a fourth proportional to the three straight lines B, C, D [6.12], so that B : C = D : E.

**Step 3.** Since A : D = D : B, the three straight lines A, D, B are proportional; therefore the rectangle contained by the extremes A, B is equal to the square on the mean D [6.17].

**Step 4.** Since A, B are rational straight lines commensurable in square only, the rectangle A, B is medial, and the side of the square equal to it is a medial straight line [10.21]. But the square on D is equal to the rectangle A, B (Step 3); therefore D, the side of that square, is medial.

**Step 5.** Since B : C = D : E, and the first, B, is incommensurable in length with the second, C (Step 1), the third, D, is also incommensurable in length with the fourth, E [10.11].

**Step 6.** Again, since the four straight lines B, C, D, E are proportional, the squares on them, being similar figures similarly described on proportional straight lines, are also proportional: sq(B) : sq(C) = sq(D) : sq(E) [6.22]. And sq(B) is commensurable with sq(C) (Step 1); therefore sq(D) is commensurable with sq(E) [10.11].

**Step 7.** By Steps 5 and 6, D and E are commensurable in square [D10.1.2] but incommensurable in length; that is, D, E are commensurable in square only.

**Step 8.** D is medial (Step 4), and E is commensurable with D, namely in square (Step 6); but a straight line commensurable with a medial straight line is medial [10.23]. Therefore E is also medial.

**Step 9.** Therefore D, E are medial straight lines commensurable in square only. It remains to show that the rectangle contained by D, E is medial.

**Step 10.** Since B : C = D : E (Step 2), alternately B : D = C : E [5.16].

**Step 11.** Since A : D = D : B (Step 2), inversely B : D = D : A [5.7].

**Step 12.** The ratios D : A (Step 11) and C : E (Step 10) are each the same as the ratio B : D; therefore D : A = C : E [5.11].

**Step 13.** Since the four straight lines D, A, C, E are proportional, the rectangle contained by the extremes D, E is equal to the rectangle contained by the means A, C [6.16].

**Step 14.** But A, C are rational straight lines commensurable in square only (Step 1); therefore the rectangle A, C is medial, that is, it is equal to the square on a medial straight line [10.21]. The rectangle D, E is equal to the rectangle A, C (Step 13), and therefore equal to that same square [CN1]; hence the rectangle D, E is also medial.

**Step 15.** Therefore medial straight lines D, E, commensurable in square only, have been found which contain a medial rectangle, namely the rectangle D, E. Q.E.F.

Note on path: the three rational straight lines commensurable in square only are taken as data set out at the start (as in 10.27, where two such lines are set out); no separate construction of them is invoked, so the proof cites no result for their existence.
